Battle Creek trucking, warehousing company expands to add capacity for local manufacturers

# Battle Creek trucking, warehousing company expands to add capacity for local manufacturers

by WWMT

Tue, September 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM

Updated Thu, October 1, 2026 at 11:46 AM

5 VIEW ALL PHOTOS

Every product on a West Michigan store shelf, every component that rolls into an assembly plant, and every pallet staged for a customer order shares one thing in common: Someone had to move it, and someone had to store it. Freight is the quiet infrastructure underneath nearly every business in the region, and when it works well, almost no one notices it at all. 

For Behnke Logistics and Behnke Warehouse, that invisible work has been the family business in Battle Creek since 1926. The Behnke way can be traced back nearly a century, to a time when Michigan's road network was still being paved and hauling freight meant a handshake, a single truck, and a reputation you could not afford to damage. Four generations later, under the leadership of owner Ben Behnke, the trucks are different, the technology is unrecognizable, and the map has grown considerably, but the operating principle has not changed.

# Inside Our New 210,000 Sq. Ft. Deltaport Warehouse

 by Bill Heaney | Logistics 

Every hour a container sits is an hour of cost. Demurrage clocks, per diem charges, congested truck gates, and long drayage runs to inland warehouses all quietly erode margin on freight that has already crossed an ocean. For importers moving volume through the Pacific Gateway, the distance between the terminal gate and the first set of dock doors matters more than almost any other variable in the inbound supply chain.

That is exactly the gap our newest facility closes. As of August 1, 2026, 18 Wheels Warehousing and Trucking has taken possession of a 210,000 square foot distribution facility at 3995 27B Avenue in Delta (Tsawwassen), positioned directly adjacent to Deltaport, Canada's primary container terminal. It is one of the shortest drayage moves available to shippers arriving through Metro Vancouver, and it is now part of our national network.

# Davidson Logistics opens new warehouse in Bridgeton 

Davidson Logistics celebrated the grand opening of its new warehouse in Bridgeton on Thursday.

By First Alert 4 Staff

Published: Oct. 8, 2026 at 6:44 PM CDT

BRIDGETON, Mo. (First Alert 4) - Davidson Logistics celebrated the grand opening of its new warehouse in Bridgeton on Thursday.

The opening marks the latest step in the company’s expansion, which began more than 40 years ago. Davidson provides delivery and inventory services to major companies, including General Electric and Boeing.

The new warehouse is part of the company’s broader expansion plans. Its president says future contracts with Boeing could allow Davidson to hire as many as 200 workers.

 Posted in Kenosha County Economic Development 

A Delavan-based third-party logistics and fulfillment company has significantly expanded its Midwest warehouse capacity after moving into a new distribution facility in Kenosha.

G10 Fulfillment now occupies 315,000 square feet of a 600,000-square-foot building at 12345 38th St., just off Interstate 94. The move increases G10’s dock capacity to 65 doors from 30.

“The Midwest is probably the most important hub for us,” said co-founder and CEO Mark Becker, who was on hand Thursday for a ribbon-cutting at the facility. He pointed to the region’s freight infrastructure and its location along the trucking corridor between Chicago and Milwaukee.

Becker said the facility can handle nearly 7 acres of inventory under one roof. G10 shares the building with food manufacturer Eagle Foods.

G10 invested about $2 million in the Kenosha buildout, which Becker said covered racking, automation and staffing costs.

# TA Services expands cross-border reach with CPT, Interload acquisitions

 by trucknews.com October 7, 2026 

TA Services announced it has acquired the assets and operations of Carmen Pacheco Transportation (CPT) and Interload Forwarding (ILF), expanding its U.S.-Mexico cross-border transportation and warehousing operations.

The acquisition gives TA Services a larger presence in the key border markets of El Paso and Laredo, Texas, and includes trucking assets, five warehouses totaling more than 550,000 sq.-ft., and a roughly 10-acre truck yard.

(Photo: TA Services)

Narborough’s Translink Express Logistics has made four senior leadership appointments following a period of sustained growth. L-R Daniel Green, Shanice Walsh, Ryan Wallis and Lee Barrett.

A Leicestershire logistics firm which has grown by a record 32 per cent over the last two years has made four senior leadership appointments as it approaches its 40th anniversary.

Translink Express Logistics has promoted three members of its team to senior roles, with Lee Barrett becoming Head of Traffic; Dan Green taking up a newly created position of Head of Project Management and Shanice Walsh promoted to Head of Operations.
